title: Artificial Intelligence for Climate Change Adaptation in Sustainable Maize Production and Socioeconomic Development in South Africa: A Comprehensive Scoping Review
content: This comprehensive literature review synthesizes current evidence regarding artificial intelligence applications in climate change adaptation for sustainable maize production, with specific emphasis on South African contexts. The review employs the Arksey and O'Malley scoping framework to systematically map evidence across 76 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026. Our findings demonstrate that AI technologies include machine learning, deep learning, Internet of Things (IoT) sensor systems, remote sensing, and computer vision. These technologies have achieved meaningful maturity for practical deployment in maize production systems, delivering documented benefits including yield prediction accuracy of up to 92%, water use efficiency improvements of approximately 35%, and fertilizer use reduction of up to 25%. However, substantial barriers, spanning technical infrastructure gaps, high capital costs, limited farmer training, and inadequate long-term field datasets, currently constrain widespread adoption, particularly among smallholder farmers. The review identifies critical research gaps regarding large-scale implementations, economic impact assessments, and South Africa-specific applications, proposing strategic recommendations for researchers, policymakers, technology developers, and farming communities.
